title: Dance floors and nightclubs, the Silver Slipper
summary: He says dancers lift the players' spirit, citing the Silver Slipper in the early 1950s.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, what's the difference between a cabaret and a nightclub and a dance hall? How did he get that in?

To tell you the truth, I didn't see much difference in it. It was all in fact the same thing with chairs and tables out on the dance floor. There's a big enough space that I'm out there for you to dance. But the majority of the nightclubs now, they don't have no dancing space. You go there, they hear the band sit at the counter and drink, or you've got space in the back there where they can put chairs and tables back there. Or you go back there and sit down and drink. There's a very few places that's got bands playing for them at night that's got a dance floor.
Do you think that changes the drum in any? Not a bit.

They still play? But I'll tell you one thing it will do. When people is dancing, it gives you more spirit to play. Particularly if you see they're enjoying theirselves. But whether you just got to sit down and entertain people and all they can do is give you applause, well there's not very much spirit to it. Because some applaud and some don't. But when you see them all get out on the dance floor and you know they're enjoying yourself, and that's why that gives you a lot of spirit. Because I've noticed a difference in that. You know when I was playing at the Paddock or in fact any of them clubs on Boydman Street, and when we get away from you and play where people could dance, I noticed a big change in your spirit. But I don't know, that's kind of a dead spirit to me, simply not looking up at the musicians playing. When they get through you applaud them. There's a lot of people go to these clubs out here that wants to dance. Now we played at the Old Silver Slipple and they had a lot of dancing there one time. When Joe Conforto had it. Well we played then. Well he had a lot of dancing. He had a space ring off for the people to dance. Well that gave us the mood to play good there too. How long ago was that? Oh that was around 19, that was back in the early 50s. Nick Agriano had us in charge then. That was around about 1953 or 54, something like that. I remember that. That was before Gene Mills Band came down here, remember? They came in right behind us.
Yeah that was quite a deal with them, you remember that? Yeah. What happened?
Yeah they told me to let them go.
Yeah they flopped in that place and then made a hit at the concert, didn't they? Yeah, it was something. You remember a fellow named Foster and his brother Dude? Yeah.
